I found several GitHub issues where browser extensions caused React hydration mismatches, mostly on React 18 and 19 RC builds. Most were closed or never confirmed, so there's no single official fix.

- **Extension-injected attributes:** In discussion #72035 (Next.js 15 / React 19 RC), a ColorZilla-added attribute on the body caused the mismatch. When Colorzilla is disabled, the hydration error resolves. A workaround removes the attribute before hydration and watches for it being re-added.
- **Extension-injected scripts:** Issue #25924 (React 18.2) reports that a React DevTools extension inserted a script tag after the body, causing errors. It is still marked Unconfirmed.
- **Video Speed Controller:** Issue #31895 reports a similar error with the Video Speed Controller extension on a React 19 RC. It was Closed as not planned.
- **Plugins before head:** Issue #24430 reports that a plugin inserting a script before the head causes a mismatch. It is marked as Resolution: Backlog.
- **Expected behavior:** React's own hydration warning lists browser extensions as a possible cause. It can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which messes with the HTML before React loaded.
- **Not extension-related:** Issue #36169 (React 19.2.4, opened March 2026) describes hydration errors from a `<script defer>` inside `<head>`. It is not about extensions.
- **Related React 19 changes:** Issue #33133 (React 19.1.0) reports that `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` combined with `suppressHydrationWarning` replaces server HTML with empty content. It was Closed as not planned.

Some users reported the mismatch went away after disabling the extension, and one reported a Vue.js devtools extension as the cause. I did not check whether any of these issues have been fixed in newer React versions.

content.text:
Yes. The closest match for React 19 is facebook/react issue #31895. It reports a hydration error from the Video Speed Controller extension on a React 19 RC build with Next.js 15. The search result showed it as closed as not planned, and I didn't open the issue to confirm.

The page title says `react/react`, which is odd, so the link may redirect.

Other related issues:
- [#25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924): scripts injected by browser extensions, such as React DevTools, cause hydration errors. It was filed against React 18 and is still marked Unconfirmed.
- [#24430](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430): a plugin that injects a script tag at the top causes a mismatch. It's marked Resolution: Backlog.
- [vercel/next.js Discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035): the ColorZilla extension adds a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute to the body. This breaks hydration on Next.js 15 with React 19. Disabling the extension fixes it, and the discussion describes a workaround that removes the attribute.

There's no single official fix. React's hydration warning lists browser extensions as a known cause. The usual workaround is `suppressHydrationWarning` on the affected element, usually `<html>` or `<body>`. I haven't checked whether newer React versions changed any of this.

- [vercel/next.js Discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035)
